topic: Template Function Overloading with SFINAE for Type Compatibility
explanation: This concept demonstrates how C++ allows overloading of template functions based on different template parameter types, utilizing SFINAE (Substitution Failure Is Not An Error) to enable or disable specific overloads depending on type traits. It is used to create flexible, type-safe functions that adapt to various template parameter combinations, ensuring correct overload resolution at compile time without causing compilation errors.
example_explanation: This example defines an overloaded operator== template function for comparing reverse iterators with potentially different underlying iterator types. It uses template parameters to accept various iterator types, demonstrating how C++ templates enable generic programming. The function compares the base iterators of the reverse iterators, illustrating template parameter flexibility and how C++ handles such overloads at compile time, ensuring type safety and correctness.
